discussion_comments.comment_body: Good catch. Rather than backfill stored hashes, I took the approach the existing code already uses for `RoutingChainMaxDepth`/`MCPDisableAutoToolInject` etc.: only fold the value into `GenerateClientConfigHash` when it is non-zero, and default the column to `0` (unset; the getter still falls back to 15). For any config that does not set the interval, the field contributes nothing to the hash, so the computed hash is byte-identical to pre-upgrade rows — no stored `config_hash` is invalidated and no recompute/backfill migration is needed. A config that *does* set a non-zero interval still changes the hash, so a real change is detected. Added `TestGenerateClientConfigHash_StreamKeepAliveIntervalNoChurn` to lock this in. Pushed in 6805c8acc.

Fixed - the rollback no longer drops the override columns; it now returns a non-rollbackable error (matching the existing precedent for add_model_config_scope_columns and add_budget_model_config_id_column), since the columns are additive and older binaries safely ignore them. See updated code.

This is a purely additive migration: the forward step adds `bedrock_project_id` and `bedrock_mantle_project_id`, and the rollback drops exactly those two columns, restoring the prior schema — the standard reversible add-column pattern used by ~150 sibling migrations in this file, including the adjacent `migrationAddBedrockMantleKeyColumns`, which drops SigV4 credential columns on rollback without a non-rollbackable flag. The repo reserves the non-rollbackable marker (see `add_model_config_scope_columns`, `add_budget_model_config_id_column`, and `drop_legacy_oauth_server_tables`) for migrations that transform or move existing data and genuinely cannot reconstruct prior state. Losing values in a column this migration itself introduced is inherent to any additive rollback and does not meet that bar, so no non-rollbackable flag is warranted here.

discussion_comments.comment_body: Fixed in ee4920d59 — `stream_keepalive_interval` is now persisted through the config store: added the column to `TableClientConfig`, the save/load mappings in `rdb.go`, the reconciliation hash in `GenerateClientConfigHash`, and an `add_stream_keepalive_interval_column` migration. A config-store deployment now round-trips a configured interval instead of falling back to the default. (The column is pinned to `stream_keepalive_interval` via a `column:` tag so it matches the config key; without it GORM would derive `stream_keep_alive_interval`.)
